title: Outpatient percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
description: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is an outpatient procedure where your cardiologist uses a catheter to open blocked coronary arteries and restore blood flow to your heart. Your doctor threads a thin tube through your blood vessels, locates the blockage, and uses a balloon or other tool to clear it. Usually a stent (small mesh tube) is placed to keep the artery open. PCI provides quick relief of chest pain and prevents heart attacks. The procedure is performed in a cardiac catheterization lab while you're awake but sedated. The cost of this procedure may vary depending on the complexity involved. Categories include standard pci and complex (multi-vessel).
